newsitem.title: UK: Brady market sees buying, across-the-board gains.
newsitem.headline: Brady market sees buying, across-the-board gains.

text.p: The Brady market tone was positive on Tuesday, buoyed by U.S. fundamentals and investor demand for high-yielding assets, dealers said.
They said trade was active with two-way business as players sought to catch up after the British Bank Holiday on Monday.
"Monday saw big gains in New York and investors are seeking higher yielding assets and we saw European buying to catch up this morning,"," a dealer said.
Traders said Russian bonds in particular were looking strong.
"The imminent Moscow Eurobond in the background is lending support," a trader said.
The City of Moscow is planning to issue a Eurobond with a three-year maturity of up to $500 million. It will be Russia's first non-sovereign bond in the international capital market.
The Russian US$ was 1/8 up bid at 83-5/8 at 1100 GMT, having peaked at 84 bid in early trade.
Minfins were up across-the-board and holding gains, with MinFin 3 up 3/4, MinFin 4 up 1/2, MinFin 5 up 7/8 , MinFin 6 up 1/4 and MinFin 7 up 7/8.
Bulgaria was holding its all-time highs.
Bulgaria's IAB were up 1/2, bid at 64-5/8, after hitting an all-time high of 65 bid.
But dealers said there had been some light profit-taking on Latin American bonds -- Argentina and Brazil.
Ecuador Bradies were holding firm -- Ecuador IEBs were up 1-1/4 bid at 88-1/2, Pars were up 1/4, Discs 1/4 and PDIs 3/8.
